concepts/aberration.title: Aberration
concepts/aberration.content:
In the 1720’s, James Bradley (1692-1762) set out to measure stellar parallax
Parallax | Desmos
but instead discovered the aberration of light, a subtle annual shift in star position caused by Earth’s motion.  He never found any evidencee of parallax with the instruments of his time.
The star, \gamma-Draconis was directly overhead in London.  Over several years, he measured a motion of about 20 arcseconds.  Now this is quite large.  A star just 1 Parsec away (3.26 light years) ought move only 1 arc-second due to parallax—IF it’s lined up in the plane where earth orbits.  A parallax drift of 20 arcseconds would be 20 times closer than that.
There were other problems with the 20 arc-second shift.

It was in the wrong direction.  The angle was at maximum when it should have been at minimum and vice versa.
Every star in the same direction was affected by the same shift.

Galilean Analogy
The Galilean Analogy invokes rainfall.  If you’re standing in the rainstorm, the rainfall falls straight downward.  If you’re moving very quickly, the rainfall comes down at an angle.
Here’s the big question.  Is it an illusion?  Did \gamma-Draconis move?  We now know that it is 154.3 light-years from earth.  20 arcseconds is 20\text { seconds}*\frac{1\text{ minute}}{60 \text { seconds}}*\frac{1\text{ degree}}{60 \text { minutes}}*\frac{\pi\text{ radians}}{180 \text { degrees}}
=9.7\times10^{-5}\text{ radians} So from our point-of-view, the star moved s=r \theta = 0.01496\text{ light years}
But it didn’t move this far by traveling.  It moved this far by way of our change of perspective.
The Common Misconception
The common misconception is that there is some “illusion” involved.  There may be, but in only one sense.  When you point at the star, you are pointing towards where it was when the image formed, not at where it is now.
But “where it was when the image was formed” (See Image Location vs Simultaneous Location) is in a specific location relative to the observer.  And that “where it was” for a star as distant as \gamma-Draconis swings 0.01496 light years as earth orbits the sun.
Unfortunately, many relativists believe it is better to invoke the Meaninglessness of distant simultaneity rather than acknowledge that events actually move around in space and time whenever we change velocity.

concepts/einstein-synchronization-conven.title: Einstein Synchronization Convention
concepts/einstein-synchronization-conven.content:
It is much harder to impose synchronization of a lot of clocks than it is to acknowledge that certain events are simultaneous.  See Imposing vs. Acknowledging Coordinates.
This page currently only considers the Einstein Synchronization Procedure (ESP) for the situation where all the clocks and the synchronizing station are stationary.
Later discussion might lead to imagining what to do when the synchronization station is stationary, but the other clocks are all moving with the same velocity, or with all different velocities.
Single Radar Method
The animation Einstein Synchronization Convention | Desmos shows the original signal going out as purple round dots.  The reflection signal comes back in the form of faded blue rectangles, and the central station in the demo goes ahead and multiplies it’s time by 1.5 so that each clock sets its time to the value sent, rather than having to do an extra calculation.

Signal 1 Artifact Establishment The artifact sets time to zero, and sends out one massive signal at t=0
Signal 1 Bounce Each object (at distance r_\text{object}) in the vicinity of the artifact reflects the signal at t=r_\text{object}/c.  The reflection includes the identity of the clock to be synchronized.
Signal 1 Detection The radar system detects the bounced signal at t=2r_\text{object}/c.
Object Sync Signal The radar system sends an object identifying signal along with the time stamp t_{set}(\text{unique object})=1.5 t.
Expense The central artifact must broadcast a different value of 1.5 t for each object.  All of the clocks need to be able to detect this signal, and pick out their own identifier and its synchronizing-time from among the noise of times aimed at other clocks.

Distant Artifact Method

Signal 1 Artifact Establishment: The first signal must establish what artifact is being used.  This information must be communicated to all of the clocks before any sync procedure can begin.
Signal 2 The continuous time signal: The distant artifact must continuously broadcast a signal that states its time.
Signal 3 Radar Signal Each Clock must send a radar signal to the artifact to determine its distance.  The distance estimate will be 2 d=c\Delta t
Setting  Each clock will combine Signal 3 (adding the radar delay d/c) and Signal 2:  (the continuous time signal) to get an estimate for its current time.
Expense: Every clock has to be equipped with its own radar.  Each radar needs to have a distinct identifier to distinguish it from other radar signals.
The accuracy of the estimate depends on the motion and acceleration of the artifact and the clock.

concepts/bold-statements/numbers-are-adj.title: Numbers are Adjectives
concepts/bold-statements/numbers-are-adj.content:
Numbers really do not have any meaning unless units are put after them.
That’s not to say they cannot be approached without assigning meaning.  I have seen students happily multiply 3^{10} \times 2^{-14}  and arrive at an answer if 6\times 10^4 or 6\times 10^{24} and there might be teachers who might give partial credit for such an answer, even though it is 8 or 28 orders of magnitude too large.  Such errors are almost inevitable when numbers are treated completely in the abstract.  When units are imagined, the problem here might be interpreted as an area of a rectangle.  One would notice that 3^{10} is a very big length while 2^{-14} is an even smaller length, and so the area obtained ought to be somewhere between big and small, with the small being favored.
Moreover, the calculator does not operate on knowing the units of the numbers.  It actually does treat the numbers entirely abstractly.  It explicitly operates on pure adjectives.   This is much in the way one can know what color is obtained by combining red and green even though no object is painted this color.  Or one might combine the adjectives of thin and muscular into “wiry” without assigning the adjectives to any particular person.
Confirm for yourself:  Does 5 have any meaning at all before you imagine 5 dots, 5 arbitrary forms, 5 units of length?  In some sense it does, just as “red” has meaning, even if it is not assigned to an object.
However, if you think of the color red, you probably imagine some red surface.  Without that surface, (the noun), you can’t think of the color red, except for the sound of the word.
But let’s say you have some capacity wherein you can imagine the number 5 and the color red in an entirely abstract way.  If I had never interacted with a Large Language Model I would probably say I didn’t believe you.  However, knowing that such Artificial Intelligence can wax quite eloquently about the number 5 and the color red just by manipulation of language itself, I do understand that there could be minds out there working completely off of symbol memorization and have no internal picture of 5 or red that requires units.
That being said, physics is a regime where all numbers — even unitless ones — have distinguishable operational descriptions.  One does not obtain an angle, for instance, without imagining a radius and an arclength, or a ratio between the swept out area and the full circle.
So pedagogically speaking, it is always beneficial to think about what units are implied, even when they cancel out; see Unitlessness

concepts/bold-statements/unitlessness.title: Unitlessness
concepts/bold-statements/unitlessness.content:
Motivating Question:
Given some arc-length, s of a circle of radius r it is popular to calculate an angle \theta = \frac{s}{r} and then either say that the quantity is “unitless” because the ratio of distance/distance cancels, or to say that the quantity has units of “radians”.


                  
                  Which is correct? 
                  
                

Neither claim is incorrect.  Mathematical forms such as sine, cosine, tangent will only accept a unitless variable as their input.  They can also accept radians.




                  
                  What about degrees? 
                  
                

Degrees multiply radians by a conversion factor of
\theta_\text{degree}=\frac{180 \theta_{radian}}{\pi}
And the sine, cosine, and tangent functions can convert to a mode that accepts degrees.




                  
                  Area Ratio 
                  
                

This same angle may be described as an area ratio:  The area swept out by the arc \Delta s as compared to the area of the full circle is also \theta, having units of m^2/m^2


More to say about unitlessness
Numbers are Adjectives and even unitless quantities in physics nearly always describe something.  For instance, in the case of radians, the unit is \text{radians}= \frac{\text{meters of arc}}{\text{meter of radius}}=\frac{\text{square meters of arc}}{\text{square meters of circle}}

concepts/distinctions/imposing-vs.-ackno.title: Imposing vs. Acknowledging Coordinates
concepts/distinctions/imposing-vs.-ackno.content:
Requirement for Distant Simultaneity to be Well-Defined

A single world-line.
An event on that world-line

Requirement for Distant Simultaneity to be Imposed
Imposing a synchronization onto distant clocks is conventional and difficult to do.  See Einstein Synchronization Convention
Given a single observation at any instant from any Point-of-View, Distant Simultaneity is perfectly well defined globally.
However, one does not, instantaneously create a universe full of physical Synchronized Clocks in that instant.  Ghost Clocks, yes, but physical clocks, no.
Simultaneity is established globally, though not imposed globally from a single point of view at a single instant.
Imposing a synchronization is different from acknowledging simultaneity. 
Imposing synchronization can be done in a small region. even with clocks that are not comovig with the synchronizing signal.
Non-inertial signal sources don’t do a very good job of Imposing synchronization over large regions.  
ECI imposes sync on the scale of earth and its satellites.  Earth’s trajectory is fairly straight on the scale of hours or days.

concepts/distinctions/invariant-and-rela.title: Invariant and Relative Quantities
concepts/distinctions/invariant-and-rela.content:
Velocity is a “relative” or “perspectival” quantity while events, themselves, such as a clock ticking a certain quantity, is called an invariant quantity.  Relative quantities are quantities that can be changed by changing your perspective, without touching or communicating an object.  Invariant quantities are things you can’t change without touching or influencing the object having the measured property.  In general the existence of an event cannot be changed, but it’s location in time and space is
Can You Make it Go Away?
You can tell if something is relative or absolute by considering whether you can “make it go away”.  The clock having a reading of \tau=3:00\ PM is something you could ignore, but if it has that time, your ignorance of it doesn’t influence the truth of the reading.
However, if the clock is passing by at 1\ m/s you can make that velocity essentially “go away” simply by walking along with it at the same speed.
If you have the means to boost yourself to arbitrary velocities, you can, without touching the clock, make it so that from your own perspective, the clock may have any velocity you want (up to the speed of light.)
”Without Touching It”
Some might object, saying “But I could take out the clock’s batteries, or stop its pendulum so that it doesn’t read 3 PM.  So can you make the reading go away?  Yes, but once you touch the clock, you’re creating other events that no one else can make “go away” unless they can physically pre-empt or undo your act.

concepts/distinctions/known-and-unknown-.content:

Local and Global Mapping

Consider the position of a vertically thrown ball in gravitational field g described by
y(t)=y_0+v_{y0} t - \frac{1}{2}g t^2
With y_0 represents the height of the ball, and v_{y0} being the vertical velocity of the ball we can say a great deal about the ball’s position, but there are things outside the domain.
Outside the domain:

Before the ball was thrown
After the ball is caught or hits the ground.

In a great many cases, the domain of applicability of the Zoom-In Principle and the domain of where a function is known is the same.

concepts/distinctions/local-and-global-m.title: Local and Global Mapping
concepts/distinctions/local-and-global-m.content:
The Lorentz Transformations are a Global Mapping.  They take all of the events in space and time as the Domain and map them to all events in space and time as the Range.  It might be worth applying a Zoom-Out Principle describing the perspectival changes of Lorentz Transformations to compare to the Zoom-In Principle applied in modeling physical changes due to laws of mechanics.
On the other hand, the metric tensor g_{\mu\nu} is a local mapping, taking, for example a tiny interval, (d\tau, dr, d\phi)  and mapping it to (dt,dx,dy) in such a way that either the Minkowski Metric is conserved, or that a Lagrangian, Action, and Euler-Lagrange Equations is conserved.

concepts/distinctions/objective-and-subj.title: Objective and Subjective
concepts/distinctions/objective-and-subj.content:
“Objective” and “Subjective” are both Homonyms.  Confusing the definitions can result in rhetorical flourishes that end in unnecessary claims of meaninglessness.
Example:
🟠JL(3305.10): "As the [[Abbreviations|ETETE]] proves if the [[Abbreviations|SOL]] is invariant, although simultaneity can be consistently defined within one [[Abbreviations|IRF]], it loses its "objective meaning" because it becomes observer dependent."
The conclusion appears compelling until we ask:

Which definition of objective is being used?


Objective

(Definition 1) not influenced by personal feelings or opinions in considering and representing facts. Contrasted with subjective.

“an objective judgment”


(2) not dependent on the mind for existence; actual:

“An objective reality”





Observer Dependency is Objective
Observer dependency satisfies both definitions of objective.  Consider the following examples:





















Perspective 1Perspective 2A person steps on an antAn ant gets stepped onOne person sees events A and B are simultaneousAnother person sees events A and B are not simultaneousAcknowledging that a fact depends on perspective does not make that fact subjective.
The perspectives themselves may differ, but the relationships within each perspective remain factual.
A velocity-dependent simultaneity relation is still objectively determined once the velocity has been specified.
Simultaneity is not an opinion
Simultaneity is not influenced by personal feelings or opinions. Is simultaneity dependent on mind?   Distant Simultaneity is fully determined by the instantaneous velocity of the chosen Point-of-View.   A mind can choose which velocity to consider, but once that choice is made, the simultaneity of relation follows as a matter of fact.
No additional opinions are required

Subjective

(1) Influenced by personal feelings, tastes, or opinions.

“his views are highly subjective” ·


(2) dependent on the mind or on an individual’s perception for its existence.



Neither definition describes simultaneity.
Simultaneity does not change because someone changes their opinion.
Nor does simultaneity cease to exist when nobody observes it.
Perspective is not Perception
A common confusion occurs when perspective is conflated with perception.
A reference frame is a perspective.
An opinion is a perception.
These are not the same thing.
Simultaneity requires a perspective, but it does not require actual perception.
It is determined by the geometry of spacetime and the chosen state of motion, not by the beliefs of an observer.
Simultaneity is not based or influenced on personal feelings, tastes, or opinions. Except that we can imagine different points-of-view, simultaneity is not ifluenced by mind.
Simultaneity is well and fully defined by a velocity of a single point-of-view.  It requires perspective, but not actual perception.
Conclusion
The statement

“Simultaneity loses its objective meaning because it is observer dependent”

works rhetorically because it quietly shifts between different meanings of objective.
Observer-dependent does not imply opinion-dependent.
Frame-dependent does not imply mind-dependent.
Before declaring a concept “subjective,” “non-objective,” or “meaningless,” it is worth pinning down exactly which definition is being used.

concepts/temporal-facing/1st-and-3rd-per.title: 1st and 3rd Person
concepts/temporal-facing/1st-and-3rd-per.content:
There are two main ways of thinking of Rotation and Boost.
We can use our muscles to influence what our avatar does:  I can, for instance, induce my avatar to rotate or accelerate by using my muscles.  When I turn right, the universe around me appears to turn left.  Hence a rotation transformation might have two different domains, depending on the context.
If I turn left, everyone sees this rotation and says “his avatar turned left”(or more likely “he turned left”.  The domain of the rotation operation was all of the “me”-particles.  Nothing else in the universe was influenced.
However, from my perspective it is exactly the opposite.  When I turn left, the only particles that weren’t affected by my rotation were the “me”-particles.  My own avatar doesn’t change position with respect to myself.  Instead, every other point in the universe was influenced by my rotation.
Likewise, when I accelerate, everyone else in the universe only sees my particles undergo acceleration, but from my Point-of-View every particle in the universe has changed velocity.

concepts/temporal-facing/avatar.title: avatar
concepts/temporal-facing/avatar.content:
In video games an “avatar” is frequently introduced, using definition 2 of the following choices:
Avatar: Dictionary definition:

a manifestation of a deity or released soul in bodily form on earth; an incarnate divine teacher.
an icon or figure representing a particular person in a video game, internet forum, etc.:

Special Relativity needs to expand this definition, or find another word to represent the figure that actually is a particular person in the real universe.

An avatar is a person or drone occupying a Point-of-View, at an event he/she/it defines as here and now. In the real universe, there is some sense by which we are each avatars carrying our own consciousness.

concepts/temporal-facing/boost.content:

Matrix Forms
These boosts take the velocity v_\eta=c\tanh\eta and render it stationary (v_\eta'=0), and take the velocity v_0=0 and send it to v_0'=c\tanh(-\eta).  If the domain is all of space and time, it means we are changing our perspective to that of an avatar (See 1st and 3rd Person) moving to the right with velocity v_\eta.  If the domain is the avatar itself, we should use the inverse transformation.

All coefficients of the transformation matrix areunitless.  These units do not actually, in any sense cause time to become space, (See Avoid Conflation, and Unitlessness). concepts/temporal-facing/descriptive-and.title: Descriptive and Perspectival Transformations
concepts/temporal-facing/descriptive-and.content:
A perspectival transformation is one that imagines “what would the situation look like from that perspective”?
The main perspectival transformations are

Rotation: (imagines the perspective of someone who has turned or turned around)
Galilean transformation (imagines the perspective of someone traveling at a different velocity)
Lorentz Transformations (imagines the perspective of someone traveling at a different velocity)

While both the Galilean and Lorentz Transformations are described the same way, here, they are different models and expectation of what the different perspective ought look like.
Descriptive transformations, on the other hand may

Polar to Rectangular Transformation: (converts cartesian coordinates to angle and radius)
Spherical to Rectangular Coordinates (converts Cartesian coordinates to yaw (polar), pitch (azimuthal) and distance)

Noninertial transformations could be in part perspectival and in part descriptive.

Rindler Coordinates: May imagine the view of an observer on a Born Rigid accelerating rocket.  Or the view of an “instantaneous boost:  See Lorentz Transformations”
Rotating coordinates: Generally imagines the view of a person standing at the center of a rotating disk, keeping his eyes on a point on the rotating disk, OR imagines a distant object moving along a straight line as he turns his head to follow it.

concepts/temporal-facing/distant-simulta.title: Distant Simultaneity
concepts/temporal-facing/distant-simulta.content:
As for whether simultaneity describes the real world, it’s much like asking whether “in front of you” describes the real world.
“In front of you” is not the same as “in front of me”, but both describe the real world.
It is exactly the same with simultaneity, except for one major issue:
In the following sense, simultaneity MAY not describe the real world—and that is in the exact same sense that the future may not describe the real world. Only past events ct < -|x| are unchangeable reality. Simultaneous events are among those that may be changeable, but not by the observer. ct>|x| are events in the future that we might influence. The graph, Causality Structure | Desmos  including an oscillating speed of light for funsies:

Only past events are unchangeable reality;
Simultaneity and “the future” are ways we talk about the world, not structures the world is obliged to honor invariantly.
But even so, the coordinates of these will-they-won’t-they-happen events is perfectly well defined, once the observer’s “here and now” is defined..
It is just whether they will happen or not that we cannot know (immediately).

concepts/temporal-facing/euclidean-point.title: Euclidean Points and Parallel World Lines
concepts/temporal-facing/euclidean-point.content:
Euclid defined

A point is that which has no part.


By this, he meant that a point has no spatial extent in any direction.  It has

no width,
no height,
no breadth

However, if his analysis were updated with regards to Special Relativity, two properties actually ought to be added to the definition
Euclid’s points also had:

Temporal Extent: Euclid’s points never vanished in the instant their position was determined
A Stationary Property: Euclid’s geometry is built on points, lines, and arcs drawn on a static medium.  They never moved around the page.

Hence in terms of Special Relativity, Euclid’s points are Parallel World Lines:
Parallel World Lines
Compare to Metric Isoclines

concepts/temporal-facing/point-of-view.title: Point-of-View
concepts/temporal-facing/point-of-view.content:
An ideal eye or camera is a point of view.  The eye or camera may be moved around, so it’s world-line is not necessarily straight.  However at any given moment it’s motion is well defined.  One way of thinking of the camera or eye is as an Avatar or a “figure representing a particular person” in reality.
In order to obtain the coordinates of events relevant to the eye or camera, one must perform the Lorentz Transformation that renders the camera’s current velocity equal to 0.  With this in mind, the correct perspectival distances and times are given at the origin, when

Here:  (x'=0) The spatial coordinate of the camera from the camera’s point-of-view is “here”, which puts the camera at the origin.
Now: (t’=0) The temporal coordinate of the camera from the camera’s point-of-view is “now”, which puts the camera at the origin.
Stationary’ v'=0 The velocity of the camera from the camera’s point-of-view is zero.  Even if the camera may be under acceleration, it’s current velocity is zero.

Exceptions:
One can describe moving points in space (see Ghost Clock) which are traveling faster than the speed of light, and in such a case, they do not describe any point-of-view.
The Logic

There are some who argue that a point-of-view under acceleration ought to observe something different than one who occupies the same position at the same time as an inertial observer with the same velocity.  As for what difference it makes though, they tend to fall silent.
What would be different?  An accelerating point-of-view would see something different immediately before and immediately after the “here and now” event.
What else would be different?  An accelerating point-of-view would experience certain stresses that an inertial observer wouldn’t experience.  Large stresses might warp a camera lens.  A non-ideal camera might change velocities between the time the light entered the lens to the time that it registers on the photosensitive plate.
What would NOT be different  The instantaneous geometry of the situation is the same for the accelerating point-of-view and the inertial point-of-view.  Except for internal forces that would mangle the camera, the observations of the global coordinates must be the same.
Conclusion: Observation of distant events is wholly determined by instantaneous position, instantaneous time, and instantaneous velocity of the point-of-view.  It is not a function of acceleration.  All observers sharing the same point at the same time having the same velocity observe the same coordinates for all events.

Relevance
This will render all events in the Spacetime to the correct perspectival distances from “here” and times from “now”.
The events most relevant to the point-of-view are those who are currently being seen.  The spatial coordinate of the Image of an object with a given world-line, is the location where that world-line intersects the past light-cone of the
Clarification: Two observers at the same point in space and time, but having two different velocities share the same past light-cone, so the locus of events observed by each is the same.  However, they do not see these same events at the same coordinates.  They also share the same future light-cone.  So, for instance, if the two particles collide, light from that collision would share the same locus of events as well.

concepts/temporal-facing/rapidity.title: rapidity
concepts/temporal-facing/rapidity.content:
Standard rapidity is associated with

a timelike worldline of velocity v or
a Lorentz boost to velocity v.

Mathematically \operatorname{rap}(v,c)=\left\lbrace\begin{matrix}\operatorname{arctanh}\left(\frac{v}{c}\right), &v<c\\\operatorname{undefined},&v>c\end{matrix}\right.
And it’s inverse \beta=\frac{v}{c}=\tanh{\eta}\\v=\beta c=c\tanh\eta
Implicit Abstraction
The “timelike worldline” and “Lorentz boost” descriptions are abstract in the following ways.

A world-line need not have any particle occupying it’s position in order to be defined.
A Lorentz boost does not require any observer or avatar actually existing or changing speed at the origin.
The timelike restriction requires that v\in(-c,c), (which in turn puts constraint on \beta\in(-1,1), but little restriction on the rapidity:  \eta\in(-\infty,\infty) .

Chrono-rapidity and Choro-rapidity
If we do not have a particle traveling with velocity v, we can define rapidity based on any space-time interval:
An interval is defined by two events \boxed{E_1=(x_1,t_t)}\text{ and }\boxed{E_2=(x_2,t_2)}
And defining \boxed{\Delta x=x_2-x_1}\text{ and }\boxed{\Delta t=t_2-t_1}
This interval exists between every pair of points, and do not have the pre-requisite that anyone associates the event-pair with a velocity.
\operatorname{rap}(\Delta x,\Delta t)=\left\lbrace\begin{matrix}\eta_\tau=\operatorname{arctanh}\left(\frac{\Delta x}{c\Delta t}\right),&|\frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t}|<c\\\eta_\chi=\operatorname{arctanh}\left(\frac{c\Delta t}{\Delta x}\right),&|\frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t}|>c\\\eta_c=\pm\infty,&\frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t}=\pm c\end{matrix}\right.
The extra notation suggests the following terms

Chrono-Rapidity Rapidity, \eta_\tau associated with a time-like interval.
Choro-Rapidity Rapidity, \eta_\chi, associated with a space-like interval
Photo-Rapidity Infinite rapidity, \eta_c associated with a speed-of-light interval.

We should not be too alarmed at putting \infty into the range of possible rapidities.  It is not remarkable that the slope of a vertical vector may be infinite.  (See Putting Infinity in the Range of Arctan).
Effect of Lorentz Boost

A Lorentz chrono-boost L(\eta_\tau) will render the events associated with the timelike interval L(\eta_\tau):(\Delta x, \Delta t)\to(0,\Delta t') That is, after the boost, the two events will happen at the same place, at different times.
A Lorentz choro-boost L(\eta_\chi):(\Delta x,\Delta t)\to(\Delta x',0) That is, after the boost, the two events will happen at different places, at the same time.
A Lorentz photo-boost \lim_{\eta_c\to\pm\infty}L(\eta_c):(\Delta x,\Delta t)\to(0,0) That is, given a photon emission and reception events, even separated by billions of light years, a sufficiently large boost can bring those two events into virtual contact.

Conflation
(See Avoid Conflation)
Rapidity and Velocity should not be conflated.  Though there is a range of velocities where this approximation holds:
\frac{v}{c}=\beta\approx\eta
Even up to 40% of the speed of light, only a 6% difference when considering the approximation that \beta\approx\tanh(\beta)

concepts/temporal-facing/spacetime.title: Spacetime
concepts/temporal-facing/spacetime.content:
The revelation that we can convert time into space is not novel or new—it is called "movement".  By changing your velocity \Delta v and then waiting \Delta t, one arrives at another location.
A common “explanation” of Special Relativity is to invoke “Spacetime” by saying “We now understand that space and time are the same.”  However Conflation of two easily distinguished ideas does not actually have much in the way of explanatory power.
Distances still have units of distance.  Times have units of time.
What is novel and new with regards to Special Relativity is the precise mechanism (Lorentz Transformations) by which someone changes their velocity and waits.
